quest.title: Fortune-Mocking Pedigree
quest.description: As night passes and you awaken next to the bonfire, you realize that Paimon is missing. As you search for her, you come upon a wandering father by chance...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x775, Mora x31175, Hero's Wit x3, Mystic Enhancement Ore x5

talks.objective: Look for Paimon inside the house

dialogues.speaker: Intimidating Man
dialogues.text: Halt! What do you think you're doing!?

choices.text: Agh!

response.speaker: Intimidating Man
response.text: This place is not whatever you think it is... Nor should you be poking your nose into my business! Begone!

choices.text: Whoa, whoa... Just calm down.

response.speaker: Intimidating Man
response.text: Your travel companion? ...You mean the one that was keeping watch by your side last night?

response.speaker: Intimidating Man
response.text: Your companion departed for the forest early this morning. That much I saw with my own eyes.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (I thought so... Still, I don't know if I can trust this person's word just yet.)

choices.text: So you mean to say that...

response.speaker: Intimidating Man
response.text: What business is that of yours? All you need to know is that I claimed this place first — and what I do here is none of your concern.

response.speaker: Intimidating Man
response.text: Do I make myself quite clear? Leave!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (There's something strange about this person. I need to find out what he's hiding...)

response.speaker: Intimidating Man
response.text: Well? What are you waiting for?

choices.text: I don't think I'll have much luck trying to find my companion in the woods...

response.speaker: Intimidating Man
response.text: *sigh* If you must... Suit yourself.

response.speaker: Intimidating Man
response.text: I've been observing you, and you don't look like a Forest Ranger, nor someone from the Akademiya.

response.speaker: Intimidating Man
response.text: Still, I'm warning you, no funny business. Promise me that, and you can do as you please.

choices.text: I'm no villain.

response.speaker: Intimidating Man
response.text: Okay, fine, whatever... Move aside. I'm heading in.

choices.text: May I join you?

response.speaker: Intimidating Man
response.text: You...

response.speaker: Intimidating Man
response.text: *sigh* Oh, go on then, have it your way. I knew I wasn't going to be able to hide this anyway. Just come in.

response.speaker: Intimidating Man
response.text: But no overreacting to anything you see in here, okay? You understand me?

choices.text: Relax. I've been around, it takes a lot to faze me.

response.speaker: Intimidating Man
response.text: Come on, then.

choices.text: Got it.
I was out here all night. I'm cold.
Nor will I pretend to be a saint.
I think I'm better off waiting here for them to come back.
You were nearby last night?
I'm only here to look for my traveling companion.
You startled me!
A hilichurl?

response.speaker: Intimidating Man
response.text: Mind your own business. Don't worry, he isn't aggressive...

response.speaker: Intimidating Man
response.text: ...How could he be. He was too young for anything like that.

response.speaker: Intimidating Man
response.text: So don't you lay a finger on him. Just find yourself a corner to rest if you're tired or cold.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: You're... from Khaenri'ah, aren't you?

response.speaker: Intimidating Man
response.text: Huh?

response.speaker: Intimidating Man
response.text: You know Khaenri'ah... Who are you, exactly? And how do you know I'm from Khaenri'ah?

choices.text: I'm just a traveler.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Your clothes...

response.speaker: Intimidating Man
response.text: Do you worship a god, Traveler?

choices.text: I follow no god. In fact, I count some of them as my foes.

response.speaker: Eide
response.text: ...Sounds like you've had an eventful life. Alright, well... my name is Eide. And you are correct — I was once Khaenri'ahn.

response.speaker: Eide
response.text: I apologize for my earlier hostility. But you must understand... As far as I'm concerned, humans who do not worship The Seven are nigh extinct...

response.speaker: Eide
response.text: ...And all who place faith in the gods are my enemies.

choices.text: That sounds a little too black-and-white.

response.speaker: Eide
response.text: ...That may be, but the fact is that chances to talk to people like yourself have been few and far between since the cataclysm.

response.speaker: Eide
response.text: This wretched curse of immortality... Who knows how long I must continue to suffer like this?

choices.text: What is the curse of immortality, exactly?

response.speaker: Eide
response.text: The curse? Huh, it was a little gift given to the people of Khaenri'ah by those vile gods...

response.speaker: Eide
response.text: We lost our home, our loved ones, everything... The agony of the cataclysm itself was already too much to bear... but then came the curse, robbing us any chance of release.

response.speaker: Eide
response.text: All we can do is watch helplessly as our souls erode and our bodies decay.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (So Eide is just like Dain, someone who bears the curse of immortality.)

choices.text: So why did some people turn into hilichurls...

response.speaker: Eide
response.text: Because although Khaenri'ah began with a single bloodline, it was a home to others, too...

response.speaker: Eide
response.text: Any who forsook their gods and came to Khaenri'ah were welcomed as our fellow citizens.

response.speaker: Eide
response.text: When the cataclysm came, we pure-blood Khaenri'ahns were declared the "greater sinners." Upon us, the gods placed the curse of immortality...

response.speaker: Eide
response.text: But those whose ancestry belonged to the domains of other gods were punished with the curse of the wilderness as they fled, turning them into monsters.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: So... who is this hilichurl to you?

response.speaker: Eide
response.text: He is Caribert... my illegitimate son.

response.speaker: Eide
response.text: *sigh* How times have changed. I can say that out loud with no consequence now, but... it was once a matter of unspeakable shame.

response.speaker: Eide
response.text: I was a noble of Khaenri'ah by blood... but I resented the life that my family had arranged for me.

response.speaker: Eide
response.text: Then one day, I met a beautiful woman amongst the people. Her roots were in Mondstadt... but that mattered not to me. It was love at first sight.

response.speaker: Eide
response.text: ...Caribert faced great hardship from the very moment of his birth, all due to my selfish desires... and I was never able to be there by his side for any of it.

response.speaker: Eide
response.text: ...After all that, he turned into a hilichurl right before my very eyes.

response.speaker: Eide
response.text: I always owed him much, and now... at least I can finally be close to him.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: ...What happened to his mother?

response.speaker: Eide
response.text: She was...

response.speaker: Eide
response.text: ...*sigh* We were separated. I do not wish to dwell on it.

choices.text: I'm sorry...

response.speaker: Eide
response.text: ...It could be worse. I suffer the pain of loss because I once had everything I could wish for.

response.speaker: Eide
response.text: And now... now that I have lost almost everything, the little that remains I see with new clarity.

response.speaker: Eide
response.text: If nothing else... At least I still have Caribert.

choices.text: What do you plan to do now?

response.speaker: Eide
response.text: Ah, yes, that reminds me. I only returned here to check on Caribert, but I do have other things I wish to do... You may come with me, if you're so inclined.

choices.text: What were you planning to do around here?
I know this must cause you great pain.
...While you were afflicted by this curse instead?
I take it that's how you've survived for so long?
Spoken like a true Khaenri'ahn.
I follow no god. Though I count some of them as my friends.
I've met others from Khaenri'ah.
Why do you keep a hilichurl at home?

dialogues.speaker: Eide
dialogues.text: We're here. Let's begin...

dialogues.speaker: Eide
dialogues.text: Wait a moment... Hey, what was that? ...Caribert?

choices.text: What!?

response.speaker: Eide
response.text: Oh no... He must have left while we were too busy preparing the medicine to notice...

response.speaker: Eide
response.text: Come on! We have to catch up with him!

choices.text: He left the house?

dialogues.speaker: Eide
dialogues.text: This is the method for making the medicine. You just need to follow the steps.

talks.objective: Synthesize the Nameless Taboo Medicine of the Royal Court

dialogues.speaker: Eide
dialogues.text: Over here.

choices.text: A Crafting Bench?

response.speaker: Eide
response.text: I'm sure you're wondering why I brought Caribert here, to Sumeru.

response.speaker: Eide
response.text: Well, it's because he needs a medicine that can only be made here...

response.speaker: Eide
response.text: One which will help him to recover his clarity of mind.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Recover his clarity of mind?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (When we were in The Chasm, Dain said that the curse could not be undone... Is recovery really possible?)

response.speaker: Eide
response.text: I do not hope to break the curse. I am well aware of my powerlessness against the punishment of the gods.

response.speaker: Eide
response.text: But it's said that this medicine is imbued with the power of Sumeru's God of Wisdom, and can awaken the mind from a state of deep stupor... It has been used in the past to treat cases of mania.

response.speaker: Eide
response.text: I believe that it might just work...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Where did you hear of this?

response.speaker: Eide
response.text: ...I read about it in a book from the Royal Library of Khaenri'ah. It was banned, since this medicine requires the power of The Seven to work.

response.speaker: Eide
response.text: In my youth, I—I disliked the life of nobility, and craved excitement. I was leafing through some forbidden texts and happened upon it.

choices.text: You know, there must've been a reason it was banned...

response.speaker: Eide
response.text: ...What other choice do I have? What exactly would you have me do?

response.speaker: Eide
response.text: The gods have already punished us! What does one more sin matter now?

choices.text: Alright, don't get too worked up...

response.speaker: Eide
response.text: Never mind, as long as you understand... I—I'm sorry, I struggle to take control of my mood sometimes... Perhaps a consequence of having lived too long.

response.speaker: Eide
response.text: As it happens, I am in dire need of some help to make this medicine.

response.speaker: Eide
response.text: My hands don't have the dexterity they once did. I fear that they may be decaying from within... all thanks to this curse of immortality.

response.speaker: Eide
response.text: Okay, to start with, take this ingredient...

choices.text: A mushroom?

response.speaker: Eide
response.text: Also, do you have any of Sumeru's regional specialties on hand? I believe they're called... <color=#00E1FFFF>Kalpalata Lotuses</color> and <color=#00E1FFFF>Sumeru Roses</color>.

choices.text: I've never seen a mushroom of this kind before...
I understand. No matter what, you have to try.
It sounds dangerous...
What are you going to use this for?

dialogues.speaker: Eide
dialogues.text: Is it done? Splendid, let me see...

dialogues.speaker: Eide
dialogues.text: Hmm. In all honesty, I do not know what the end product is supposed to look like. The banned book didn't feature any illustrations...

dialogues.speaker: Eide
dialogues.text: ...Well, the moment has finally arrived... Curses.

choices.text: Excuse me?

response.speaker: Eide
response.text: No, no. We need to perform one final step to complete the medicine.

response.speaker: Eide
response.text: I said before that this medicine relies on the power of the God of Wisdom for its restorative effects...

response.speaker: Eide
response.text: Which means... we must pay a visit to a Statue of The Seven.

choices.text: Ouch... that can't be easy for someone from Khaenri'ah...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (Since he needs the God of Wisdom's power, should I get Nahida to help?)

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (...Forget it. Eide hates the gods — it could complicate things. I'll just do it his way.)

response.speaker: Eide
response.text: Let's go. Bring the medicine with you.

choices.text: I understand your reluctance.
Is it time to give Caribert the medicine?

talks.objective: Go to the nearby Statue of The Seven

dialogues.speaker: Eide
dialogues.text: Look at this statue... How can I bow before this thing...

dialogues.speaker: Eide
dialogues.text: God of Wisdom. Look at me.

dialogues.speaker: Eide
dialogues.text: I will utter no prayer, nor will I sing your praises.

dialogues.speaker: Eide
dialogues.text: You and your kind destroyed my home, wrought unfathomable suffering on my compatriots... Yet here I stand before you.

dialogues.speaker: Eide
dialogues.text: You cannot mock me more than fate itself already has.

dialogues.speaker: Eide
dialogues.text: God of Wisdom, I seek not to disavow myself of the sinful blood that flows through my veins. I wish only to beseech you to have pity upon a young and unfortunate soul.

dialogues.speaker: Eide
dialogues.text: My son, Caribert... He was turned into a monster before he had the chance to witness anything beautiful in this world... This is no fate for a child.

dialogues.speaker: Eide
dialogues.text: If everything the gods have done was in order to have the impious people of Khaenri'ah bow their heads...

dialogues.speaker: Eide
dialogues.text: Then... I bow to you now.

dialogues.speaker: Eide
dialogues.text: I have given up all I ever stood for...

dialogues.speaker: Eide
dialogues.text: All I ask for is a tiny miracle. For Caribert to see this world once more.

dialogues.speaker: Eide
dialogues.text: Please, god... I beg of you.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (I may not know the whole truth behind the cataclysm, but the people of Khaenri'ah have truly suffered...)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Why could Khaenri'ah and The Seven not coexist in peace?)

dialogues.speaker: Eide
dialogues.text: I have made quite enough of a fool of myself for one day. Let's go.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Things will get better.

talks.objective: Administer the dose of medicine to the hilichurl

dialogues.speaker: Eide
dialogues.text: Caribert?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (The hilichurl seems almost lifeless. Its reactions to everything are incredibly weak...)

dialogues.speaker: Eide
dialogues.text: Well, we've prepared the medicine. We might as well try it.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: With your help, Eide feeds the newly made medicine to the hilichurl.

dialogues.speaker: Eide
dialogues.text: Caribert? It's me... It's your father. Caribert?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Anything?

dialogues.speaker: Eide
dialogues.text: Caribert... Please, say something.

dialogues.speaker: Eide
dialogues.text: I'm sorry I couldn't be at your side when you were born... and that I failed to reach you and mama in time when you both were suffering...

dialogues.speaker: Eide
dialogues.text: But I'm here now. Papa's been by your side all these years. I've never left you. Not once.

dialogues.speaker: Eide
dialogues.text: Are you still angry with me, Caribert?

dialogues.speaker: Eide
dialogues.text: I know you're awake now... Do you not want to talk to me?

dialogues.speaker: Eide
dialogues.text: I'm so sorry, Caribert. Forgive me, please! Say something. Anything!

dialogues.speaker: Eide
dialogues.text: Please... please...

choices.text: Eide, stop...

response.speaker: Eide
response.text: Aah!

response.speaker: Eide
response.text: Gods above! What more do you want from me!?

response.speaker: Eide
response.text: You took everything from here, and I still bowed to you!

response.speaker: Eide
response.text: I'd give you my very life if only you cared to take it! But you won't even let me die!

response.speaker: Eide
response.text: ...I knew it. I should never have trusted anything that had to do with the gods. I was just deluding myself...

response.speaker: Eide
response.text: The gods of this world have never stood with humanity... Not even for a moment!

choices.text: Calm down, Eide.

response.speaker: Eide
response.text: Other reasons... What do you mean?

choices.text: Such as... who knows, perhaps the dosage was too low.

response.speaker: Eide
response.text: Huh... you really think so...?

choices.text: You have to exhaust all options...

response.speaker: Eide
response.text: Give up? No, no. Never! ...Yes, you're right. I cannot let myself wallow in despair.

response.speaker: Eide
response.text: Even if I must stay here with him for... fifty years? A hundred? What difference does it make? I do not lack for time...

choices.text: That's the spirit.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (To have infinite time, yet no hope... can only be called torture.)

response.speaker: Eide
response.text: Let's go. We'll make another dose.

response.speaker: Eide
response.text: The most crucial ingredient in this medicine is the unusual mushroom, which makes things complicated... but not impossible.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Where did you get those mushrooms from, anyway?

response.speaker: Eide
response.text: I grow them. In that field.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Wait, in a field? Like a crop?

response.speaker: Eide
response.text: ...The details don't matter, right? Curb your curiosity and just do as I instruct — if you truly wish to help me, that is how you can do it.

response.speaker: Eide
response.text: There is a waterfall near the statue I prayed at. I need you to collect some water from there around two in the afternoon.

response.speaker: Eide
response.text: I'll be here watching Caribert. Once you're back, I will make some fertilizer for the mushrooms.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Got it.

response.speaker: Eide
response.text: Good. Then please head over when the time comes.

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: Time passes quickly. Before you know it, it is two in the afternoon...

choices.text: Fine.
I'll keep helping you.
Unless you are ready to give up on Caribert...
Or maybe it takes a full course of treatment.
There might be other reasons it didn't work.
It didn't work.

talks.objective: Go to the waterfall to fetch some water

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Eide carefully waters his field...

dialogues.speaker: Eide
dialogues.text: I need you to stand guard here for a while. Whatever you do, don't let any Forest Rangers approach the house. Understand?

choices.text: Of course...

response.speaker: Eide
response.text: Good. I'll be back soon, the fertilizer won't take but a moment to make.

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: You wait in the field for Eide to return. After a while...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (Monsters! And so many of them... It looks like they're coming for this field...)

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (Does watering the field somehow attract monsters? Hmm, better fend them off.)

choices.text: Your secret is safe with me.

dialogues.speaker: Eide
dialogues.text: What happened? Was it monsters?

dialogues.speaker: Eide
dialogues.text: Thank goodness you were here. I couldn't have taken them on all by myself... I'd have to hide and wait until they were gone.

dialogues.speaker: Eide
dialogues.text: Oh yes — I've got the fertilizer. The effects can take some time to kick in, so let's get on with it.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Eide spreads the fertilizer evenly. Before long, the elemental energy within starts to take effect...

dialogues.speaker: Eide
dialogues.text: Next, we pick the mushrooms and repeat the same steps as before to make another dose. I trust you still remember the method?

dialogues.speaker: Eide
dialogues.text: Ah, you're back. Caribert's condition is stable...

dialogues.speaker: Eide
dialogues.text: By which I mean... he still isn't responding.

dialogues.speaker: Eide
dialogues.text: Anyway. Give me the water.

talks.objective: Synthesize the Nameless Taboo Medicine of the Royal Court

choices.text: Eide, the medicine's ready.

response.speaker: Eide
response.text: Oh! Uh, sorry, I just... After resting in this field for a while, my thoughts began to wander...

response.speaker: Eide
response.text: I have been so very weary, for many years... if only I could fall asleep here in this field, and never wake up again...

choices.text: But though the curse denies you even this...

response.speaker: Eide
response.text: Hehe, I do indeed, that's why it was just a fleeting thought... Thank you for your help once again. Now for the final step... Back to the Statue of The Seven.

choices.text: You still have Caribert.
Hey, stop daydreaming...

talks.objective: Go to the nearby Statue of The Seven

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I've picked some before, yes.

dialogues.speaker: Eide
dialogues.text: Wonderful. I—In that case, we have everything we need.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: No, but I can go out and get some.

dialogues.speaker: Eide
dialogues.text: Could you really? Much obliged.

dialogues.speaker: Eide
dialogues.text: Without your help, goodness knows how long this would take me...

dialogues.speaker: Eide
dialogues.text: Thank you.

dialogues.speaker: Eide
dialogues.text: Please fetch the water. I'll be waiting here.

dialogues.speaker: Eide
dialogues.text: *sigh* I suppose I will soon have to visit the Statue of The Seven once more...
